A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Equivariant Splitting study, with complete main text and Appendices A–C. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable comparison of the equations, figures, tables and proofs.

before.justification: v5 reports original experiments on compressive sensing, image inpainting, MRI and CT in Section 5, plus supplementary experiments and analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v6 retains the original quantitative experiments and reconstruction examples in Section 5, together with the supplementary empirical results in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same splitting losses, equivariant reconstructors, training procedure and inference averaging. The corrected argument notation in Theorem 3 does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MNIST, DIV2K, fastMRI and LIDC-IDRI coverage, including real MRI measurements, noise-dominated MRI, push-broom inpainting and the supplementary Gaussian simulation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including supervised learning, EI, MC/SURE and the applicable incomplete-image, pseudo-inverse, IDFT or FBP baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B retain identical data splits, preprocessing, masks, noise levels, model configurations, training settings and PSNR/SSIM/EQUIV evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The architecture ablations, nearly equivariant push-broom-mask test, unknown-noise tests, MAP-equivariance verification and training-trajectory analysis are unchanged in Section 5.5 and Appendix B.4.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same average ± standard deviation reporting. No seed information, repeated-training run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted curves and qualitative reconstruction findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 reports ES PSNR of 28.54 ± 2.75 dB for synthetic MRI at ×8 acceleration and 40 dB SNR in both versions.

T1.justification: Theorem 3 changes f(A,x) to f(y,A) in Section 4.3 and Appendix C, aligning its notation with the existing Definition 1. Its premise, conclusion in Equation 21 and proof remain substantively identical; no mathematical reasoning changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about single-operator self-supervision, equivariant reconstructors, MMSE optimality and empirical performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning learned equivariance, computational efficiency, transformation selection, noise sensitivity and failure with nearly equivariant operators remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The algorithms, hyperparameters, architecture details, hardware disclosures and training-duration information are unchanged. Both versions provide the same code link and reproducibility statement.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and positioning relative to measurement splitting, equivariant imaging and equivariant networks are identical.

P1.justification: Theorem 3’s argument notation is corrected from f(A,x) to f(y,A) in both occurrences. The arXiv stamp changes from v5 dated 10 March 2026 to v6 dated 12 May 2026; the remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8, Tables 1–10 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same displays, captions, formatting and placement. The notation and version-stamp edits leave the page organization unchanged.

improvement.justification: v6 fixes a small notation inconsistency in both statements of Theorem 3. Definition 1 and the unchanged proof already establish the intended meaning in v5, so this correction and the version-stamp update have negligible effect on overall quality. The scientific content, supporting evidence and reproducibility information are unchanged.
